summary: SIEM failure-mode mapping after tenant credential rotation and legal evidence handoff
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported gaps in SIEM ingest following a scheduled tenant credential (KEK) rotation. The gaps overlap with a legal evidence request window and the customer requires a verifiable handoff (signed manifest + per-batch checksums) for the impacted time range.

Impact: Missing or duplicate events in Novus Financial's Splunk/Kafka bridge for ~2026-03-09T22:00 to 2026-03-10T03:30 UTC. Customer is enterprise with contractual evidence SLA; potential regulatory exposure if requested retained events cannot be proven.

Environment: prod-us-east; tenant id: tenant-novus-prod; export path: s3://redwood-audit-exports/novus/2026/03/09-10

Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger scheduled KEK rotation on a staging tenant following same rotation order; 2) Request incremental SIEM delta for the rotation window; 3) Observe temporary exporter errors (403/401) then replay/resume tokens misalign on downstream HEC/Kafka connector.

Observed logs/behaviour: export-service returned transient 401s between 2026-03-09T22:15 and 22:42 UTC; exporter worker retried with exponential backoff and eventually succeeded for most batches but two sequence windows show missing sequence numbers and resume-token mismatch. Downstream Splunk HEC shows duplicate sequence entries for a small subset (correlated by event.uuid).

Customer requested deliverables: - Signed per-batch manifest for the requested window (ed25519) - Resume tokens and proof of non-deletion for any missing events - Walkthrough playbook showing credential rotation order and failure modes
investigation_notes: Initial triage: SRE confirmed KEK rotation occurred 2026-03-09T22:05 UTC; rotation order followed expected steps but there was a ~30s delay applying new exporter client certs on 2 of 6 exporter pods.

Hypothesis A: exporter client certs expired for in-flight connections causing 401s and partial batch writes. Hypothesis B: resume-token checkpointing raced with the rotation and advanced without persisting a small tail of events.

Collected evidence: exporter logs (exporter-logs-2026-03-09.tar.gz uploaded to private artifacts), S3 delta index for tenant-novus-prod, HEC ingest metrics showing spike in 4xx at 22:15–22:42, and resume-token timeline from the scheduler trace.

Correlation: two missing sequence windows align with the pods that had delayed cert reload; both resumed successfully but the local in-memory checkpoint skipped a final flush due to a race with shutdown handler.
Customer communication: asked for signed manifest and assurance that missing events were not deleted; provided preliminary timeline and asked for extraction by 2026-03-12 to meet legal review.
Mitigations applied: exporter pods patched to block new rotation if active flush count > 0; added synchronous checkpoint on graceful shutdown in canary branch (PR linked).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a tenant in a sandbox that mirrors prod exporter count and rotation cadence.
2) Seed high-throughput export traffic for an hour to populate exporter buffers.
3) Trigger KEK/client cert rotation from orchestration (mimic timeline: rotate keys then rotate exporter certs with 30s stagger).
4) Monitor exporter logs, S3 delta index, and resume-token values; look for 401 spikes and sequence gaps.

customer_updates: 2026-03-10: Acknowledged receipt of timeline and requested signed manifest + proof-of-non-deletion. Customer confirmed legal review kickoff on 2026-03-13.
2026-03-11: Shared interim findings and ETA for signed bundle (target 2026-03-12 end of day).
2026-03-12: Customer asked to include per-event uuids that map to missing sequence windows.
actions_taken: 1) Opened internal hotfix PR to add synchronous checkpoint flush on graceful shutdown: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892
2) Generated per-batch manifest for 2026-03-09T21:50 -> 2026-03-10T04:00 and signed with infra-ed25519 key (artifact uploaded to secure bucket).
3) Produced resume-token timeline export and attached mapping of event.uuid -> s3-object for all events in the window.
4) Started on playbook document describing rotation failure modes and recommended rotation gating; draft shared to Confluence.
resolution: Workaround and evidence handoff delivered: Signed manifest (ed25519) and resume-token timeline provided to Novus Legal on 2026-03-12. Hotfix merged to trunk (PR 4892) and scheduled for canary deploy 2026-03-13. Root cause: race between exporter shutdown handler and checkpoint persistence during staggered cert reload. Permanent fix: ensure synchronous flush before cert reload and add rotation pre-check for active flush operations.
postmortem_followups: Create a pre-rotation checklist in the rotation orchestration to prevent cert reload while exporter buffers are non-empty.
Add an automated test that simulates in-flight rotation and validates checkpoint persistence.
Update SIEM onboarding playbook to request rotation window notice from customers when legal evidence windows overlap.
Retention: confirm artifact storage for signed manifests is retained for 12 months and accessible to compliance reviewers.
